Consult Summary:
- 31-year-old with 4 days of intensely pruritic, sore, red rash on chest, hands, and flexural elbows; history of eczema; likely eczema flare. 

History:
- Presenting complaint: 4 days of very itchy, sore, red skin rash on chest, hands, and inner elbows; significant sleep disturbance and difficulty concentrating at work; interferes with hiking.
- Associated symptoms/ROS: Skin cracking in some areas. Denies bleeding, discharge, fever, respiratory symptoms, bowel or urinary issues. No facial involvement.
- Pertinent negatives: No known triggers identified; no recent product or clothing changes reported.
- Past medical history: Prior eczema (previously limited to arms). Asthma in the past (currently inactive).
- Medications tried: Prior prescribed eczema cream and shower additive (previously effective, not now). OTC “steroid cream” from pharmacy last night (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) without relief. Antihistamines tried recently without benefit (specific agent/dose/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social history: Lives with flatmates; employed as a project manager at a pharmaceutical company; nonsmoker; drinks a few beers per week.

Examination:
- Vitals: 
- Examination findings: Clinician reports visualizing the rash via teleconsult; described as “familiar” in appearance (no specific descriptors documented).

Impression:
- Likely eczema (atopic dermatitis) flare.

Plan:
- Topical corticosteroid: Prescribe a stronger topical steroid (specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Emollients: Prescribe/use emollients, including in bath/shower; use regularly for 7–10 days before judging effect (specific product/dose/frequency not documented).
- Antihistamines: May use OTC options (e.g., loratadine, chlorpheniramine/Piriton). Offer prescription for fexofenadine (dose/frequency not documented).
- Trigger management: Keep a diary of potential triggers (e.g., clothing, soaps, shower gels); consider modifications if correlations identified.
- Follow-up: Return next week if not improving.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Detailed skin exam description (morphology, distribution, extent/BSA), vitals, exact medication names/doses/routes/frequencies, guidance on steroid potency/application and duration, infection screen signs (e.g., weeping, crusting beyond patient report), documentation of eczema severity scoring, family history of atopy, occupational/irritant exposures, skincare routine specifics.
● Internal conflicts: Duration noted as 3 vs 4 days (patient states 4 days). Distribution mentioned by clinician as “chest and back,” while patient reports chest, hands, inner elbows (no back involvement) — conflict noted. Patient addressed as “sir” earlier and later as “Sarah” — conflict noted.
● Transcript quality: Audio intermittently unclear with inaudible segments; some statements partially unintelligible.
